cost_basis.cheapest_design: Cheapest design that still does the job. Two designs cost nothing per run. (1) A chance formula written into the rule by the rules writer (p = 0.03 x days since service): the rule language has no arithmetic between two values (docs/plans/ai_judge.md Decided 3), so it would need a language change of its own. (2) Declared bands: the rule's ordinary checks choose among literal chances the rules writer writes (sawmill: under 5 days since service 0.05, 5 to 9 days 0.2, 10 or more 0.4), drawn against the same run seed; no arithmetic, no estimator, no Jev call, and a literal chance is the path the rule's {use: value} fallback already takes, so E1 gets bands with no new code. Against bands: every number is the rules writer's guess fixed at build time, the facts count only at the band edges, the numbers multiply with the facts (3 facts in 3 bands each is 27 chances to write and check), and Brian asked for rules that propagate based on Jev. That is an argument about fit, not proof, so E1 measures it as variant (d) of the plain-version comparison (one rules-writer call, measured median $0.0021): if the bands and Jev's chances differ by no more than 0.1 on at least 8 of the 10 cases, E2's rules-writer instructions prefer bands for a chance that depends on one or two facts and keep Jev for the rest (Q88). Jev costs under $0.001 per 30-day run with the per-run cache (one call per distinct question and inputs), reads only the declared fields, and needs no language arithmetic. Chosen: Jev with the per-run cache, with declared bands as the cheaper rival measured in E1 (inferred by agent, 2026-11-10). The binding constraint is latency, not cost (measured, ~/projects/data/llm_observability.db, 2026-11-10): successful Jev calls averaged 0.43 s (99th percentile 2.8 s), but 6.6% of calls failed, provider errors after 0.89 s and network errors after 20.2 s on average. With a 5 s timeout per try and one retry (plan Decided 7), an estimate takes about 0.933 x 0.43 + 0.037 x (0.89 + 0.43) + 0.029 x (5 + 0.43) = 0.61 s on average (computed) and at most 10 s before its fallback, about 18 s for a 30-day run; without the timeout about 1.05 s, about 32 s per run (Q85). For the judge's stopping point, a Jev chance question would cost about 1/50 of the judge's $0.0016 per check; that option is recorded for the judge plan's J5 (Q86), not taken here.

stage_effects.stage: per-run cache: one Jev call per distinct question and inputs (E1)
